subsystem: Screen Companion (desktop bubble, follow, look-now, screen drawing, dictation, hotkeys)
summary: The Screen Companion is a large, carefully built feature: a hidden always-on-top bubble that F8 opens for screen help or dictation, a drawing layer (Ctrl+Alt+D), Celine marking things on your screen by herself, and a bubble that follows your cursor (Ctrl+Alt+F). The logic is well tested here (about 135 focused tests pass), but every Windows piece (WebView2 window, hotkeys, overlay, follow, dictation) has only ever run against fakes and has never been tried on your laptop. It only works in resident mode and only after Setup-Apex-Screen-Companion.cmd has installed pywebview. One real regression: adding the draw/follow hotkeys made F8 stop being swallowed, so F8 now also reaches whatever app you are in.

gaps.issue: F8 is no longer a 'private' Windows hotkey. Since Ctrl+Alt+D and Ctrl+Alt+F were added to the same hotkey manager, F8 goes through pynput instead of Windows RegisterHotKey, so F8 is NOT swallowed: the app you are in also receives F8 (Excel/Word: extend-selection mode; VS Code and browser dev tools: debugger resume), including the very field you are about to dictate into. A clash with another program owning F8 is also no longer detected.
gaps.evidence: app/hotkey.py:116-121 (RegisterHotKey path only when exactly ONE binding); agent/desktop_companion.py:183-189 binds F8 + Ctrl+Alt+D + Ctrl+Alt+F on one GlobalHotkeys; introduced by commit 0486195
gaps.fix_hint: Give F8 its own GlobalHotkeys instance (or teach GlobalHotkeys to use WindowsFunctionHotkey for each bare F-key binding and pynput for the rest), and add a test that F8 still takes the RegisterHotKey path when draw/follow hotkeys are also bound.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read app/hotkey.py:116 and agent/desktop_companion.py:184-189; ran a python snippet building the binding dict from config defaults: 3 bindings -> RegisterHotKey condition is False. The only real-key test (tests/test_screen_companion_desktop.py:261) binds a single <f24>, so nothing covers the 3-binding case.

gaps.issue: The desktop Companion is 'on by default' but cannot start unless Setup-Apex-Screen-Companion.cmd was run: pywebview is only in requirements-screen-companion.txt, and Start-Apex-Platform/install-apex.bat never install it. Without it the window never starts and F8, Ctrl+Alt+D and Ctrl+Alt+F are never bound (they are bound only after the pywebview check). It is reported in the live status and hardware check, but nothing on the dashboard or in the launcher tells you.
gaps.evidence: config.py:417 (COMPANION_DESKTOP_ENABLED default True); agent/desktop_companion.py:162-163 raises before hotkeys are bound at :179-189; requirements.txt has no pywebview (only requirements-screen-companion.txt:2); install-apex.bat:39; mitigations agent/live_status.py:162-163, tools/hardware_check.py:361-369
gaps.fix_hint: Have Start-Apex-Platform print one clear line ('Desktop Companion not installed: run Setup-Apex-Screen-Companion.cmd') when find_spec('webview') is None, or bind F8 anyway with a fallback to the browser Companion.
gaps.how_confirmed: Grepped requirements*.txt and install-apex.bat for webview; read the order of the find_spec check vs. hotkey binding in agent/desktop_companion.py:155-189; read the live_status and hardware_check messages that do surface it.

Ctrl+Alt+D / Ctrl+Alt+F pressed while the desktop window is still (re)starting can be silently lost: 'activate' events are held until the page is ready, but 'sketch' and 'follow' events are processed at once, the error is only logged to desktop.log, and the event is marked done.
gaps.evidence: app/companion_desktop.py:530-534 (activate waits for bridge._ready) vs :580-599 (sketch/follow do not); after = item['seq'] at :609
gaps.fix_hint: Treat 'sketch'/'follow' like 'activate' (break and retry) until bridge._ready is set.
gaps.how_confirmed: Read the command loop; whether the page is usually ready before a user presses the key depends on timing I could not reproduce.

The owner appears to use deepseek-flash; the provider adapter sends the screenshot as an OpenAI-style image_url part. docs/DEEPSEEK.md claims image support, but nothing here proves the live API accepts it; if it does not, every F8 screen-help turn fails.

needs_from_owner: Run Setup-Apex-Screen-Companion.cmd once (if you have not), then start with Start-Apex-Platform.cmd; check %LOCALAPPDATA%\Apex\Companion\desktop.log for errors.
Run Test-Apex-Hardware.cmd and confirm the 'Companion window and hotkeys are installed' line and the display-scale line.
Press F8 over another app: bubble appears beside the pointer, microphone prompt appears once, Celine describes the right screen. Note whether F8 also did something inside that app (e.g. Excel/Word).
Ask Celine 'where is the Save button?' during F8 help: does an arrow appear on the right spot and does the bubble fly to it?
Press Ctrl+Alt+D: drawing layer opens; draw, undo, save an SVG, Done. Press Ctrl+Alt+F: bubble toggles between cursor and corner.
Pick 'Dictate' in the bubble, click a Notepad field, press F8, speak, pause: text should type in; switch field and confirm it stops.
Confirm deepseek-flash actually accepts screenshots (an F8 turn that answers about the screen, not an error).
Tray Mute, then press F8/Ctrl+Alt+D: nothing should start. Unmute.
On your 125%/150% laptop screen, check the bubble does not land off-screen or under the taskbar.

rating.why: Well designed and heavily unit-tested, but every Windows-facing part is untried on the laptop, needs a separate setup, and F8 regressed to a non-swallowed key.
